ResearchTabDef.label: Roman
ResearchTabDef.generalTitle: The arts of the Roman state
ResearchTabDef.generalDescription: The state arms factories, the drill and kit of the legions, Roman masonry and the ceremony of the imperial court.

ResearchProjectDef.label: military dress
ResearchProjectDef.description: The long-sleeved tunic and the fibula-pinned cloak that mark a man as a soldier of the late Roman army.

ResearchProjectDef.label: fabricae
ResearchProjectDef.description: The state arms factories of the empire, each making one kind of weapon to a standard pattern: the long spatha, the hasta, the lead-weighted plumbata and the javelin.

ResearchProjectDef.label: signa militaria
ResearchProjectDef.description: The standards of the units: the draco wind-sock, the labarum with the Chi-Rho, around which a unit rallies and for which it dies.

ResearchProjectDef.label: painted scuta
ResearchProjectDef.description: Large oval shields of glued planks, rimmed with rawhide and painted with each unit's own blazon.

ResearchProjectDef.label: ridge helmets
ResearchProjectDef.description: Helmets of two iron halves joined by a ridge, quick to make in the fabricae, and the segmented spangenhelm learned from the steppe.

ResearchProjectDef.label: lorica hamata
ResearchProjectDef.description: The ringmail shirt of the legions: thousands of riveted and punched rings, long and heavy, but proof against cuts.

ResearchProjectDef.label: ballistarii
ResearchProjectDef.description: Handheld torsion crossbows, the arcuballista, in the hands of the ballistarii.

ResearchProjectDef.label: lorica squamata
ResearchProjectDef.description: Armour of overlapping bronze or iron scales sewn to a backing: stiffer and showier than mail.

ResearchProjectDef.label: clibanarii
ResearchProjectDef.description: Heavy cavalry clad head to foot in iron, after the Persian fashion, charging with the long kontos.

ResearchProjectDef.label: parade arms
ResearchProjectDef.description: Gilded helmets set with glass stones and gilded spathae for the emperor's guard and the generals.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Roman masonry
ResearchProjectDef.description: Walls of dressed stone with courses of brick, laid in lime mortar; columns turned from a single block.

ResearchProjectDef.label: limes fortifications
ResearchProjectDef.description: The fortifications of the frontier: high curtain walls with a wall-walk and battlements behind which archers can stand.

ResearchProjectDef.label: imperial court
ResearchProjectDef.description: The ceremony of the sacred palace: the throne raised on marble, the purple, and the statues of the emperors.

ResearchTabDef.label: Barbarian
ResearchTabDef.generalTitle: The crafts of the free peoples
ResearchTabDef.generalDescription: The skills of the Germanic and steppe peoples: weaving and smithing, shields of lime wood, timber halls, and the trappings of kingship.

ResearchProjectDef.label: tablet weaving
ResearchProjectDef.description: Wool and linen woven on the warp-weighted loom, edged with tablet-woven bands: tunics, cloaks, hoods and caftans of the peoples of the north and the steppe.

ResearchProjectDef.label: palisades
ResearchProjectDef.description: Ditch and bank crowned with a palisade of sharpened logs; timber walls; tents for the war band on the move.

ResearchProjectDef.label: village smithing
ResearchProjectDef.description: The village smith's work: seaxes long and short, the bearded axe and the throwing axe, the framea spear, and leather caps.

ResearchProjectDef.label: war banners
ResearchProjectDef.description: The banners and totems of the peoples, carried before the war band.

ResearchProjectDef.label: lime-wood shields
ResearchProjectDef.description: Round and oval shields of lime-wood boards covered in hide, with an iron boss, painted in each people's colours.

ResearchProjectDef.label: spangenhelms
ResearchProjectDef.description: Helmets riveted from iron segments in a frame, with cheek guards and sometimes a mail curtain.

ResearchProjectDef.label: the angon
ResearchProjectDef.description: A heavy throwing spear with a long iron shank and a barbed head: it pins an enemy's shield and drags it down.

ResearchProjectDef.label: great halls
ResearchProjectDef.description: Halls on stone footings, dry-stone walls, and the four-wheeled wagons of a people on the move.

ResearchProjectDef.label: mail byrnies
ResearchProjectDef.description: A shirt of mail, the byrnie, worth a farm; and lamellar armour of laced iron plates, learned from the steppe.

ResearchProjectDef.label: pattern welding
ResearchProjectDef.description: Rods of iron and steel twisted and forged together into blades that shimmer like snakeskin: the swords of chieftains, the long rhomphaia, the great axe.

ResearchProjectDef.label: kingship
ResearchProjectDef.description: The ring-giver's trappings: gilded helmets and swords, purple cloaks, noble shields, and the high seat at the head of the hall.

ResearchTabDef.label: Persian
ResearchTabDef.generalDescription: The dress and arms of the Sassanid empire, its armoured cavalry, its brick-and-stone fortresses, its fire temples and the court of the King of Kings.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Persian dress
ResearchProjectDef.description: Belted tunics and long riding coats of patterned silk and wool, and the Phrygian cap.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Persian smithing
ResearchProjectDef.description: Long straight swords with scabbard slides, the gorz mace and the tabarzin axe of the horseman.

ResearchProjectDef.label: derafsh
ResearchProjectDef.description: The standards of the army, and above all the Derafsh Kaviani, the jewelled banner of the kings.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Persian shields
ResearchProjectDef.description: Round shields of wood and hide, the tall wicker spara of the infantry, painted with stars and sacred fire.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Persian helmets
ResearchProjectDef.description: Tall segmented helmets with a mail aventail.

ResearchProjectDef.label: clibanarii
ResearchProjectDef.description: The heavy cavalry of the Sassanids: helmets with a face of mail, men like statues of iron on armoured horses.

ResearchProjectDef.label: the Immortals
ResearchProjectDef.description: The guard of the King of Kings, whose number is always kept full: gilded helmets and shields.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Sassanid masonry
ResearchProjectDef.description: Walls of fired brick on stone footings, stepped battlements and ribbed curtain walls.

ResearchProjectDef.label: fire temples
ResearchProjectDef.description: The fire altar, the atashdan, in which the sacred fire of Ahura Mazda is kept burning day and night.

ResearchProjectDef.label: court of the King of Kings
ResearchProjectDef.description: The crown with the winged globe, the royal robe and the golden throne behind the curtain.
